faq.intro: Answers about El Tintal, the geospatial data, the maps and the project.

q1.q: What is Get to Know Your Neighborhood: El Tintal?
q1.a: An academic web platform to learn about the places, history and data of the El Tintal neighborhood: 14 modules with a map, list, photos and ratings.

q2.a: In western Bogotá D.C., within the Kennedy locality. Main roads such as Avenida Ciudad de Cali and Avenida de las Américas run through it.

q3.q: Where does the data come from?
q3.a: From open sources: OpenStreetMap (queried with Overpass and Nominatim), the Bogotá open data portal and datos.gov.co. Each record keeps its source and whether it was verified.

q4.q: What do “to be verified” and “sample data” mean?
q4.a: “To be verified” marks information that could not be confirmed in a public source. “Sample data” marks demo records that do not describe a real place.

q5.q: Which coordinate system do the maps use?
q5.a: WGS84 (EPSG:4326), the same as GPS: latitude and longitude in decimal degrees. Areas are shown in square meters.

q6.q: How do I use the maps?
q6.a: Drag to move, use the wheel or gestures to zoom in and select a marker to open the place card. Everything also works with the keyboard.

q7.q: Why does the theft module show no personal data?
q7.a: It only uses aggregated, anonymous data by time of day and method, to inform without exposing anyone or stigmatizing places.

q8.q: Can I add or rate places?
q8.a: Any visitor can browse and rate. Creating, editing or deleting records requires signing in with an admin account.

q9.q: How do I change the language or text size?
q9.a: The ES/EN selector is in the top bar. The accessibility bar on the right changes the text size, turns on high contrast and reduces motion.

q10.q: Who created the project and how can I contact her?
q10.a: Marie Anne Lopez Poveda, a Cadastral and Geodesy Engineering student. You can message her on WhatsApp with the button in the bottom-right corner.

flag.title: Flag of the Kennedy Locality
flag.alt: Flag of Kennedy: three equal horizontal stripes, yellow on top, white in the middle and green at the bottom.
flag.design: Three horizontal stripes of equal height. The colors yellow, white and green are confirmed by Local Decree 13 of 2021 of the Kennedy Local Mayor's Office (article 3); the stripe layout comes from Wikimedia Commons.
flag.note: we found neither the official act adopting the flag nor an official explanation of its colors, so we give no heraldic interpretation.

locator.title: Location within Kennedy
locator.label: Map of the Kennedy Locality with the El Tintal neighborhood highlighted in the northwest.
locator.definition: On this platform, El Tintal is UPZ 78 Tintal Norte (343 ha) plus UPZ 79 Calandaima (319 ha): 662 ha according to the SDP (2012), via Catastro Bogotá. It is an operational definition, not an official administrative unit. Portal Américas lies outside, about 1.3 km to the south (UPZ 83 Las Margaritas).

navigate.title: Getting around
navigate.body: The sidebar has Home, Local History and «Categories», which opens the 14 modules. Each module has a map of its places, a list with search and filters, and a detail view per place with photos, ratings and the source of every data point. On a phone, open the sidebar with the menu button.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.body: The bar on the right side makes the text larger or smaller (90 % to 125 %), turns on high contrast and reduces motion. The whole platform works with a keyboard: Tab moves forward, Shift+Tab back, Enter opens and Escape closes dialogs, the chat and notices. The first Tab offers «Skip to main content».

language.title: Language
language.body: At the top right you can switch between Spanish (ES) and English (EN). It is remembered for your next visit.

chat.title: Mini Marie, the assistant
chat.body: The button with Mini Marie, next to the WhatsApp one, opens the chat. Ask about any of the 14 modules («What schools are there?»), the best-rated place, what's nearby, how many records there are, the history or how to contact Marie. It answers with the platform's data and takes you to the section with a button.

account.title: Accounts and permissions
account.body: Without an account you can browse everything. With a visitor account, created in «Access / Session», you can rate places with stars. Only the admin account creates, edits and deletes places and photos.

data.title: Where the data comes from
data.body: Data comes from OpenStreetMap and Bogotá Open Data, and each item shows its source. «To be verified» marks what couldn't be confirmed by an official source, «Press» what comes from the media, and «sample data» the example records of modules without an open source. Here El Tintal is UPZ 78 plus UPZ 79 (662 ha): an operational definition, not an official administrative unit.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: The green WhatsApp button at the bottom right writes directly to Marie Anne Lopez Poveda, the creator. Her details are in the Creator Profile.
